_about: Public-domain Henry Newland (1804-1860), Tractarian rector of Westbourne, Sussex, and vicar of St Marychurch, Devon, for the Word Hoard: Three Lectures on Tractarianism, Confirmation and First Communion, a commentary on Philippians, a sermon on the Lord's coming, and a tract on the Manchester and Salford education scheme, with his fishing books The Erne and Forest Scenes in Norway and Sweden. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 109 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

hnewland-tractarianism: Three lectures on tractarianism : delivered in the town hall, Brighton (London, 1849)
hnewland-socinianism: Socinianism : the inevitable result of the Manchester and Salford scheme of national education, vol. Talbot Collection of British Pamphlets (London : Joseph Henry Batty, 159, Fleet Street, 1851)
hnewland-lord-at-hand: The Lord is at hand : a sermon preached at S. Peter's Chapel, Charlotte Street, Pimlico, on Friday, 14th December, 1852 (London : J. Masters, 1852)
hnewland-confirmation: Confirmation and first communion : a series of essays, lectures, sermons, conversations, and heads of catechising, relative to the preparation of catechumens (London : Joseph Masters, 1860)
hnewland-philippians: A practical and exegetical commentary on the Epistle of St. Paul to the Philippians : in which are exhibited the results of the most learned theological criticisms, from the age of the early Fathers down to the present time (Oxford : J. H. and Jas. Parker, 1860)
hnewland-erne: The Erne, its legends and its fly-fishing (London, Chapman and Hall, 1851)
hnewland-forest-scenes: Forest scenes in Norway and Sweden: being extracts from the journal of a fisherman (London, G. Routledge & Co., 1855)

_excluded.hnewland-ireland: The 1829 Apology for the Established Church in Ireland and the 1832 reply to Doyle are by Henry Newland, Dean of Ferns, a different man
_excluded.hnewland-de-dominis: The Life of Antonio de Dominis (1859) is by Henry Newland, D.D., Dean of Ferns, per its title page; a different man
